questions.q: The total area of all the bars in a histogram is directly proportional to the...
questions.explain: In a histogram, the area of each rectangular bar represents the frequency of that class. Therefore, the total area of all the bars combined is directly proportional to the total frequency of the distribution.

questions.q: When constructing a cumulative frequency curve (ogive), the cumulative frequencies are plotted against the...
questions.explain: An ogive, or cumulative frequency curve, represents the accumulation of frequencies up to a certain point. Therefore, the cumulative frequency is plotted against the corresponding upper class boundary of each class interval.
questions.exam: WASSCE Further Maths: Statistics and Probability

questions.q: To estimate the mode of grouped data from a histogram, one must...
options: find the area under the tallest rectangle
draw diagonal lines from the top corners of the tallest rectangle to the adjacent top corners of the neighboring rectangles
calculate the average of the class boundaries of the tallest rectangle
questions.explain: To geometrically estimate the mode from a histogram, one draws crossing diagonal lines inside the tallest bar (modal class), connecting its top corners to the nearest top corners of the adjacent bars. The x-coordinate of the intersection point is the mode.
questions.exam: WASSCE Further Maths: Statistics and Probability
questions.subject: Further Mathematics (Elective Mathematics)

questions.q: If the class intervals of a frequency distribution are $1-5, 6-10, 11-15$, what is the lower class boundary of the second class ($6-10$)?
questions.explain: The class boundaries close the gap between consecutive class limits. The gap between the upper limit of the first class ($5$) and the lower limit of the second class ($6$) is $1$. Half of this gap ($0.5$) is subtracted from the lower limit of the second class to find its lower boundary: $6 - 0.5 = 5.5$.
questions.exam: WASSCE Further Maths: Statistics and Probability

questions.q: In a grouped frequency distribution, the median class is $20 - 29$ with a frequency of $20$. The cumulative frequency before the median class is $20$, and the total frequency is $60$. What is the median? (Assume continuous class boundaries $19.5 - 29.5$).

questions.q: For a histogram representing data with unequal class intervals, the height of each rectangular bar is proportional to the:
questions.explain: When class widths vary, making heights purely proportional to frequencies would distort the visual representation of the area. Therefore, the frequency is adjusted by plotting frequency density (frequency divided by class width) to ensure the area of each bar remains proportional to its frequency.

questions.q: In a distribution, the lower quartile is $45$ and the upper quartile is $65$. What is the semi-interquartile range?
questions.explain:
The semi-interquartile range is given by $\frac{Q_3 - Q_1}{2}$. 
Given $Q_3 = 65$ and $Q_1 = 45$, the semi-interquartile range is $\frac{65 - 45}{2} = \frac{20}{2} = 10$.
questions.exam: WASSCE Further Maths: Statistics and Probability

questions.q:
An ogive is plotted for a set of $200$ observations.

To find the interquartile range from the graph, you would read the values on the x-axis corresponding to which cumulative frequencies?
questions.explain:
The interquartile range is $Q_3 - Q_1$. The lower quartile ($Q_1$) corresponds to $\frac{N}{4}$ and the upper quartile ($Q_3$) corresponds to $\frac{3N}{4}$. 
For $N=200$, $Q_1$ is at $200/4 = 50$, and $Q_3$ is at $3 \times 200 / 4 = 150$.
